image_description: A bright green common iguana (Iguana iguana) is positioned diagonally across a forest floor covered in brown leaves and twigs. The iguana has a prominent dorsal crest running down its spine, a long laterally compressed tail with banding, and visible limbs with clawed digits. The head features a large subtympanic shield and a visible dewlap.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is large and triangular with a prominent dewlap (loose skin fold) hanging from the throat.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head shape is clearly triangular and large relative to the body. A distinct fold of skin (dewlap) is visible under the chin/jaw area.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are large with round pupils and golden irises.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While the eye is visible, the resolution is insufficient to confirm 'golden irises' or distinct 'round pupils'. The eye appears mostly dark/black due to lighting and image quality, failing the strict color/detail requirement.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: A large circular subtympanic shield (scale) is present below the tympanum.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A large, distinct, circular scale pattern is clearly visible on the cheek area behind the jawline, matching the description of the subtympanic shield.
The torso appears thick and muscular, consistent with a robust reptilian body structure.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Coloration is bright green in juveniles, becoming darker green to greyish-green in adults with broad black bands on the body and tail.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The iguana is bright green (suggesting juvenile or sub-adult). Faint darker banding is visible on the tail and body, consistent with the species' coloration patterns.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Row of enlarged, spine-like scales running from the nape along the midline of the back to the tail base, forming a serrated crest.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A clear, serrated row of spines runs continuously from the neck down the spine to the start of the tail. This is a definitive feature of the iguana.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is covered in small, granular scales with larger, plate-like scales on the head.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The texture on the body appears granular/beaded, while the scales on the snout and top of the head appear larger and more plate-like, matching the biological description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are long and muscular with five clawed digits on each foot.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The front left limb is clearly visible, showing long toes with distinct claws. The hind limb is partially visible but shows similar structure. The anatomy appears biologically correct for an arboreal lizard.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and longer than body, used for balance and defense.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is visibly flattened from side-to-side (laterally compressed) and extends significantly beyond the visible portion of the body, consistent with the 'longer than body' trait.
